title: WPSS/1877/2016 of Naveen Singh AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1877 of 2016
Naveen Singh & another ... Petitioners
 Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others ... Respondents
Mr. Vinay Kumar, Advocate, present for the petitioners.
Mr. N.P. Sah, Standing Counsel, present for the State of Uttarakhand
Mr. N.S. Pundir, Advocate, present for respondent No. 4.
Mr. Manoj Kumar, Advocate, present for respondent Nos. 7 and 8.
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J. (Oral)
1. Heard Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for the
petitioner, Mr. N.P. Sah, Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand, Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned counsel for respondent
No. 4, Mr. Manoj Kumar, learned counsel for respondent Nos. 7
and 8 and perused the records.
2. By means of this writ petition, petitioner has sought
the following reliefs:-
i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
certiorari calling for the records and quashing the
selection of the private respondents on the post of
Assistant Teacher L.T. Grade Hindi (60%) against the
vacancies for general category inasmuch as the
meritorious reserved category candidates (OBC) who have
obtained more marks on their own merit, than the cut of
marks, have not been shifted against open category
vacancies as per mandate of Section 3(6) of 1994 Act.
ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondent Uttarakhand
Technical Education Board/Examining Body to shift the
meritorious reserved category candidates (OBC) who have
obtained more marks on their own merit, than the cut of
marks, to the vacancies of Open category on the post of
Assistant Teacher, L.T. Grade Hindi (60%) and
consequently declare the said vacancies to be filled by the
reserved category candidates belong to OBC.
iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondent Uttarakhand
Technical Education Board/Examining Body to call the
petitioners for counseling for the post of Assistant
Teacher, L.T. Grade Hindi (60%) and to recommend their
name for appointment inasmuch as the petitioners are
immediately below the last selected candidates in the OBC
category.

2
3. Case of the petitioners is that they belong to Other
Backward Class (in short 'OBC') category who applied for the
post of Assistant Teacher - L.T. Grade (Hindi) pursuant to
advertisement dated 24.02.2014. It is the case of petitioners
that out of 412 vacancies of Assistant Teacher - L.T. Grade
(Hindi) which were notified by the advertisement, 10% were
reserved for Uttarakhand Rajya Andolankari and in view of
interim order passed by Division Bench of this Court, in WPPIL
No. 67 of 2011, 41 vacancies, reserved for Uttarakhand Rajya
Andolankaries, have been kept apart and no one has been
recommended against these vacancies. It is further the case of
petitioners that out of total 412 vacancies of Assistant Teacher
- L.T. Grade (Hindi), 53 are reserved for OBC category
candidates. It is further the case of petitioners that after
leaving aside the vacancies earmarked for OBC (Women) and
OBC (Persons with disabilities) etc., only 27 vacancies are
available to the petitioners under OBC (Open) category. It is
further the case of petitioners that petitioner No. 1 scored
120.75 marks out of 200 in the written examination whereas
petitioner No. 2 scored 121.75 marks out of 200 in the written
examination. It is further pleaded in the writ petition that
score of last selected candidate in OBC (Open) category is
122.25 marks whereas the score of last candidate belonging to
General (Open) category was 132.75 in the first counseling and
thereafter it was lowered to 129.75 marks in the second
counseling.
4. Contention of the petitioners is that six candidates
(not party to the writ petition) belonging to OBC category, who
secured marks between 129.75 to 132.75 and were
recommended for the vacancies reserved for OBC category,
should have been recommended against the Unreserved
vacancies. It is the submission of learned counsel for the
petitioners that if these six candidates were recommended for

3
appointment against Unreserved vacancies, then petitioners
would have fair chance of success in the selection.
5. Mr. Vinay Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners
submits that the Selecting Body i.e. Uttarakhand Technical
Education Board (respondent No. 4.) committed illegality by
applying roster while calling successful candidates for
document verification/counseling, whereas roster should have
been applied at the time of making final recommendation for
appointment. In support of this contention, Mr. Vinay Kumar,
relies upon Rule 15(6)(one) of the Recruitment Rules of 2014.
English translation of Rule 15(6)(one) of the Recruitment Rules
of 2014, as supplied by Mr. Vinay Kumar, is being extracted
below for ready reference:-
"Application forms will be scrutinized by concerned
Additional Director, Secondary Education or Examination
Body nominated by the State Government and after
conducting the examination as provided in the Appendix,
select list of the candidates will be prepared in terms of
Rule 6, subjectwise in order of proficiency as per the
marks obtained by them. The Examining Body will make
available said select list to the Additional Director,
Secondary Education of the concerned Region. The select
list will contain the name not more than 25% of number
of vacancies. The nominated Examining Body would allot
the Regional Cadre as per the option mentioned in the
application form of the candidate, Women Branch (in case
of female candidates) and Regional General Branch
(female and male candidates). The Examining Body can
make allotment of a candidate on the second option of
Region/Branch against the vacancies in the concerned
subject to a candidate even when a candidate secures
place in the merit list, but as per his first option the

4
vacancy in the concerned Region/Branch (General or
Women) is not available."
6. Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned counsel for the Selecting
Body (respondent No. 4), on the other hand, submits that final
result in respect of selection in question was declared on
11.04.2016 and 371 candidates were declared successful for
the post of Assistant Teacher - L.T. Grade (Hindi). Thereafter
successful candidates were called for document
verification/counseling vide notification dated 11.04.2016,
which was uploaded in the website of the Selecting Body. In
the said notification, it was mentioned that successful
candidates for the post of Assistant Teacher - L.T. Grade
(Hindi) should report for counseling on 05.05.2016. He further
submits that in the said notification, roll number of 371
candidates declared successful for the post of Assistant
Teacher - L.T. Grade (Hindi), were mentioned. Sri N.S. Pundir
further submits that in the first counseling as many as 40
candidates belonging to OBC category were called for
counseling against Unreserved vacancies by virtue of their
superior merit. Thus, according to Mr. Pundir, apart from 27
candidates belonging to OBC category, who were appointed
against posts reserved for them, 40 candidates belonging to
OBC category have been appointed against Unreserved posts.
Thus, according to Mr. Pundir, contention of learned counsel
for the petitioners is without any substance. Mr. Pundir
further submits that Rule 15(6)(one) of the Recruitment Rules
of 2014, relied by the petitioners, does not support their case,
as select list has to be prepared as per merit. He submits that
reservation policy of the State Government was strictly applied
and in cases where a candidate belonging to a particular
category did not turn up for counseling/document verification,
then candidate next in order of merit, belonging to the same
category, was called for counseling/document verification.

5
Thus it is the case of Selecting Body that reservation policy and
roster have been strictly followed and grievance raised by the
petitioners is without any substance. Mr. N.S. Pundir, learned
counsel further submits that except five vacancies on the post
of Assistant Teacher - L.T. Grade (Hindi), which have been kept
reserved in terms of order of this Court, all other vacancies
have been supplied. He further submits that if the contention
of learned counsel for the petitioners is accepted, then the
entire select list will have to be revised, which shall result in
dislocation of persons who are already appointed, which will
not be proper in the absence of those persons.
7. Sri Manoj Kumar, learned counsel for respondent
Nos. 7 and 8 submits that respondent Nos. 7 & 8 belong to
General category, who have scored more marks than the last
selected candidate in General category. He further submits that
both respondent Nos. 7 and 8, have scored 130 marks each. He
further submits that respondent Nos. 7 and 8 have filed
impleadment application subsequent to the order passed by
this Court whereby five posts of Assistant Teacher - L.T. Grade
(Hindi) were directed to be kept vacant. He further submits
that large number of persons were appointed before filing of the
writ petition and no relief can be granted to the petitioners
without hearing those persons, who will be adversely affected
by grant of relief to the petitioners.
8. Assistant Teacher - L.T. Grade is a regional cadre
post, meaning thereby, they are appointed by Additional
Director of Kumaun or Garhwal Region for that region, and
they are not liable to be transferred outside the region. Cadre of
L.T. Grade teacher is divided into Women Branch and General
Branch. Only lady teachers can become member of Women
Branch while General Branch is open to persons of both
genders. Due to peculiar geographical condition of
Uttarakhand State, teachers have their own preference

6
regarding place of posting. In order to meet the aspiration of
candidates finally selected for appointment, a counseling is
held in which selected candidates are given opportunity to
indicate their preference for (i) Kumaon/Garhwal Region, (ii)
Women/General Branch and (iii) place of posting.
9. It is thus apparent that counseling is held only upon
conclusion of selection process and candidates are called for
counseling upon their final selection. In the event of a selected
candidate not turning up for counseling, the candidate next in
order of merit belonging to the same category has to be invited
for counseling to ensure that candidates belonging to different
categories get their due share. In the process, if the merit of the
last candidate belonging to General category, called for
counseling, goes lower than the cut-off-marks of the last OBC
candidate, who was called for counseling, it does not mean that
every time, the select list will have to be revised to maintain
balance between the OBC category and General category
candidates.
10. A perusal of Rule 15(6)(one) of Recruitment Rules of
2014 reveals that a subjectwise merit list has to be prepared in
the light of Rule 6 of the said Rules. Rule 6 of the said Rules
provides that reservation to candidates belonging to Scheduled
Caste, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes and
other categories, shall be given as per the Government Orders
prevailing at the time of recruitment. The select list, so
prepared, shall be supplied by the Examining Body to the
appointing authority i.e. Regional Additional Director of
Education. It further provides that the select list shall contain
names not more than 25 percent of the vacancies.
11. As far as submission of learned counsel for the
petitioner regarding Rule 15(6)(one) of the Recruitment Rules of
2014 is concerned, in my opinion, it does not support the

7
contention of the petitioners. The Selecting Body has prepared
separate select lists of candidates belonging to different
categories, and in the event of a candidate, belonging to a
particular category not turning up, then the candidate next in
order of merit from the same category, was invited. In the
absence of any contrary provision in the Recruitment Rules,
this Court is of the opinion that no fault can be found with the
act of the Selecting Body.
12. Even otherwise also, all persons appointed against
unreserved vacancies and vacancies reserved for OBC category
have scored more marks than the petitioners. The OBC
candidates, who according to petitioners are to be appointed
against Unreserved posts, are not party to the writ petition and
behind their back, no decision can be taken which may affect
their interest. Moreover, grant of any relief to petitioners will
result in disturbing the entire selection, as the entire select list
in respect of all categories will have to be revised and which is
not possible in the absence of persons who have been
appointed.

13. Thus there is no scope for interference with the
selection in question. The writ petition lacks merit and is liable
to be dismissed and is hereby dismissed. Interim order dated
20.09.2016 is vacated. No order as to cost.
(Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
19.07.2017
Aswal
